title: Understanding Field Unification, Data Model, and Application Settings

blocks.text: Field unification is the process of resolving conflicts and transforming data attributes in records merged during entity unification. Field unification is a two-step process. First, attribute reconciliation addresses conflicts in merged entity attribute values, resolving them via system defaults or source-prioritized logic. Second, attribute transformation applies business rules to classify and enrich data. To learn more, see Understanding the Data Model in the Agentic Security Operations Platform and What Is Data Unification?

In addition to field unification, the data model and grouping rules affect field values. Grouping rules update the corresponding field unification rules, and field unification rules update the corresponding rules in the data model unidirectionally.

All fields within the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform) are preconfigured with system-defined reconciliation logic in the data model. While the data model allows for advanced default value configurations, reconciliation logic can be achieved with the simple, no-code field unification rules. When you first configure field unification for a specific field, the system prompts you to unlink and override on the Data Unification - Fields page to confirm this change. This action overrides the existing data model configuration.

Creating or updating a field unification rule populates and overrides the corresponding data model logic, but any subsequent changes made to the data model's rule for that field are not reflected in the field unification rule. Always save after unlinking and overriding to confirm updates.

Agentic SecOps Platform ticket (e.g., Ticket, Violation Ticket) grouping rules are typically managed within Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) or Asset Exposure Management (AEM), but they can also be configured on the Data Unification - Fields page. When you create or update an Agentic SecOps Platform ticket grouping rule in UVM or AEM, it unidirectionally overrides the corresponding rule in field unification. This means that changes are reflected in the associated field unification rules, but not vice versa. So while it's possible to configure grouping rules in field unification and apply them to tickets, these changes won't sync back to the grouping rules setup page.

Agentic SecOps Platform incident rules are managed in Agentic SOC. When an incident is created, the associated incident rule unidirectionally overrides any field unification rules for the incident Title, Type, and Grouping Details fields.

blocks.item: Custom: Incidents created from custom incident rules, which you create and manage these rules based on your unique business objectives and threat landscape.
Platform: Incidents created from default incident rules, which are built from common use cases and industry best practices. You can modify these rules to suit your organization's needs.
AI: Incidents created by the Correlation agent. To learn more, see About Agents.
